source_text:
Ὁδοὶ δύο εἰσί, μία τῆς ζωῆς καὶ μια τοῦ θανάτου, διαφορὰ δὲ πολλὴ μεταξὺ τῶν δύο ὁδῶν.
Ἡ μὲν οὖν ὁδὸς τῆς ζωῆς ἐστιν αὕτη: πρῶτον ἀγαπήσεις τὸν θεὸν τὸν ποιήσαντά σε, δεύτερον τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν: πάντα δὲ ὅσα ἐὰν θελήσῃς μὴ γίνεσθαί σοι, καὶ σὺ ἄλλῳ μὴ ποίει.
Τούτων δὲ τῶν λόγων ἡ διδαχή ἐστιν αὕτη: εὐλογεῖτε τοῦς καταρωμένους ὑμῖν καὶ προσεύχεσθε ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐχθρῶν ὑμῶν, νηστεύετε δὲ ὑπὲρ τῶν διωκόντων ὑμᾶς: ποία γὰρ χάρις, ἐὰν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς; οὐχὶ καὶ τὰ ἔθνη τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν; ὑμεῖς δὲ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς μισοῦντας ὑμᾶς, καὶ οὐχ ἕξετε ἐχθρόν.
ἀπέχου τῶν σαρκικῶν καὶ σωματικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν: ἐάν τίς σοι δῷ ῥάπισμα εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν σιαγόνα, στρέψον αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἔσῃ τέλειος: ἐὰν ἀγγαρεύσῃ σέ τις μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετ’ αὐτοῦ δύο: ἐὰν ἄρῃ τις τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου, δὸς αὐτῷ καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα: ἐὰν λάβῃ τις ἀπὸ σοῦ τὸ σόν, μὴ ἀπαίτει: οὐδὲ γὰρ δύνασαι.
παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου καὶ μὴ ἀπαίτει: πᾶσι γὰρ θέλει δίδοσθαι ὁ πατὴρ ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων χαρισμάτων. μακάριος ὁ διδοὺς κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν: ἀθῷος γάρ ἐστιν. οὐαὶ τῷ λαμβάνονται: εἰ μὲν γὰρ χρείαν ἔχων λαμβάνει τις, ἀθῷος ἔσται: ὁ δὲ μὴ χρείαν ἔχων δώσει δίκην, ἱνατί ἔλαβε καὶ εἰς τί: ἐν συνοχῇ δὲ γενόμενος ἐξετασθήσεται περὶ ὧν ἔπραξε, καὶ οὐκ ἐξελεύσεται ἐκεῖθεν, μέχρις οὗ ἀποδῷ τὸν ἔσχατον κοδράντην.
ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τούτου δὲ εἴρηται: Ἱδρωσάτω ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη σου εἰς τὰς χεῖράς σου, μέχρις ἂν γνῷς, τίνι δῷς.
thought_title: The Two Ways and the Way of Life
orientation: The Didache opens with the Two Ways teaching, and this first section presents the way of life: love of God and neighbor, the golden rule, love of enemies, non-retaliation, and generous giving.
pass_a_gloss: Ways two there are, one of the life and one of the death, difference [there is] but much between the two ways. The [particle] then way of the life is this: first you shall love the God the [one] having made you, second the neighbor of you as yourself: all [things] but as many as you might wish not to happen to you, also you to another do not do. Of these but of the words the teaching is this: bless the [ones] cursing you and pray on behalf of the enemies of you, fast but on behalf of the [ones] persecuting you: what for grace, if you love the [ones] loving you? not also the gentiles the same do? you but love the [ones] hating you, and not you will have an enemy. Abstain from the fleshly and bodily desires: if anyone to you gives a slap on the right cheek, turn to him also the other, and you will be perfect: if presses into service you anyone mile one, go with him two: if takes away anyone the cloak of you, give to him also the tunic: if takes anyone from you the [thing] of you, do not demand [it] back: not for you are able. To everyone the [one] asking you give and do not demand [it] back: to all for he wishes to be given the father from his own gifts. Blessed the [one] giving according to the commandment: innocent for he is. Woe to the [one] taking: if [particle] for need having takes anyone, innocent he will be: the [one] but not need having will give account, why he took and for what: in distress but having become he will be examined about [the things] which he did, and not he will go out from there, until he pays back the last quadrans. But also about this [matter] but it has been said: Let remain the alms of you in the hands of you, until you know, to whom you give.

choices.why: The glossary mandates 'way' for ὁδός; the existential construction is rendered naturally in English while keeping the two ways as the subject.
The adjective πολλή modifies διαφορά; 'great' captures the magnitude of the contrast between the two ways.
The future indicative with imperative force is rendered as 'you shall love' to preserve the command-like force of the Greek future.
χάρις here means 'credit' or 'merit' in a rhetorical question; 'credit' captures the sense of something deserving recognition.

choices.english: He will be put in confinement
choices.why: συνοχή means 'confinement' or 'distress'; the passive sense of being placed in confinement fits the judicial context of examination and repayment.
The imperative ἱδρωσάτω is vivid and physical; 'sweat' preserves the metaphor of holding the coin until it is damp from the hand.

pass_b_english: There are two ways, one of life and one of death, and the difference between the two ways is great.
Now this is the way of life: first, you shall love God who made you; second, your neighbor as yourself. And whatever you do not want to happen to you, do not do to another.

This is the teaching of these words: bless those who curse you, and pray for your enemies, and fast for those who persecute you. For what credit is it if you love those who love you? Do not the Gentiles do the same? But you must love those who hate you, and you will have no enemy.

Abstain from fleshly and bodily desires. If someone gives you a slap on the right cheek, turn the other to him as well, and you will be perfect. If someone presses you into service for one mile, go with him two. If someone takes your cloak, give him your tunic as well. If someone takes what is yours, do not ask for it back, for you cannot get it back.

Give to everyone who asks you, and do not ask for it back. For the Father wants to give to all from His own gracious gifts. Blessed is the one who gives according to the commandment, for he is innocent. Woe to the one who receives: if someone receives because he has need, he will be innocent; but the one who has no need will give an account of why he received and for what purpose. He will be put in confinement and examined about what he has done, and he will not get out of there until he pays back the last penny.
But about this too it has been said: Let your alms remain in your hands until you know to whom you are giving.
notes: The source has μια for μία and τοῦς for τοὺς, minor itacisms or spelling variants common in the manuscript tradition.
The source has λαμβάνονται for λαμβάνοντι, likely a scribal error for the dative singular participle.

problems.why: Passive infinitive 'to be given' obscures that Father wants to give, not that gifts be given
problems.fix: For the Father desires to give to all from His own gifts
problems.ruling: πᾶσι θέλει δίδοσθαι = 'wants to give to all'; rendering as passive 'gifts to be given' obscures Father as active giver.

edits.old: For the Father wants gifts to be given to all from His own gracious gifts.
edits.new: For the Father wants to give to all from His own gracious gifts.

problems.quote: Let your alms sweat in your hands
problems.why: 'Sweat' is likely a literal gloss; the idiom means to hold tightly or let perspire (i.e., not give hastily).
problems.fix: Render: 'Let your alms remain in your hands' or gloss the idiom.

edits.old: Let your alms sweat in your hands until you know to whom you are giving.
edits.new: Let your alms remain in your hands until you know to whom you are giving.

fixed: Changed 'sweat' to 'remain' to render the idiom naturally while preserving the sense of holding back until discernment.

problems.why: Does not make sense in context; seems to mean 'you cannot get it back' or 'you cannot demand it.'
problems.fix: Render as 'for you cannot demand it back' or similar.

edits.old: do not ask for it back, for you cannot.
edits.new: do not ask for it back, for you cannot get it back.

fixed: The English 'for you cannot' was flagged as unclear; the source means 'you cannot get it back,' so I added 'get it back' to clarify the meaning while keeping the sentence natural.

polish.changed: Replaced the obscure 'quadrans' with 'penny' for modern readers, and clarified that the teaching in the third paragraph is the author's instruction, not a quotation.

notes.why: ‘Quadrans’ is an obscure Roman coin; readers won’t know its value.
notes.fix: Explain or replace with “the last small amount”.

notes.quote: this is the teaching of these words: bless those who curse you, and pray for your enemies, and fast for those who persecute you.
notes.why: Unclear whether these are Jesus’ words, the author’s instruction, or a quoted tradition.
notes.fix: Introduce with “According to the teaching attributed to Jesus,”.
